name: Arisai
overview: Arisai is a male figure mentioned in the book of Esther, identified specifically as the son of Haman. Beyond this familial connection, Scripture provides no additional details about his tribe, background, or personal attributes. His mention is brief and serves primarily to establish his lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Arisai appears only once in Scripture, in Esther 9:9, with no given meaning or divine origin noted. Therefore, his name is simply recognized as a proper noun without further etymological significance provided in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Arisai is explicitly identified as the son of Haman. Scripture does not record any other family relationships or connections for him beyond this paternal link.
scriptureSignificance: Arisai's significance in the biblical narrative is tied directly to his relationship with Haman, a prominent antagonist in the book of Esther. Mention of Arisai helps to underscore the familial line of Haman, which is relevant in the context of the events surrounding Haman's downfall. However, Arisai himself does not play an active role in the narrative.
